assignments.note: 2024-12 Can You Trust LLM Judgments reliability
assignments.why: Measures the reliability of LLM-as-a-judge verdicts across repeated samples with McDonald's omega (audit), and its subject is the act of LLM judging.
An agent that evaluates visual generators with tools (agentic judge) and plans each new evaluation round from the previous round's results (evaluator loop refining its tests).
Replaces static scoring with a multi-turn interview and feedback loop (alternative paradigm) run by an interviewer LLM acting as the evaluator.
A meta-evaluation benchmark measuring whether PRMs and critics find the earliest wrong step, so it audits process reward models.
Executable software-engineering task environments for agents, used to train outcome verifiers on agent trajectories.
A leaderboard measuring how well models judge creative writing (separability, stability, self/family bias), i.e. a meta-evaluation of LLM judges.
Chooses rule-based accuracy and format rewards over a neural reward model to avoid reward hacking (reward-model design for training), a verification-based signal rather than a judge scoring outputs.
A thinking-LLM judge that plans then executes its evaluation, trained by iterative DPO self-training on synthetic preference pairs.

assignments.note: 2025-01 Exploring and mitigating adversarial manipulation of voting-based leaderboards
assignments.why: Studies attacks on Chatbot Arena's pairwise voting leaderboard and their mitigations, i.e. manipulation of an arena's vote aggregation.

assignments.note: 2025-01 Improving your model ranking on Chatbot Arena by vote rigging
assignments.why: Shows strategic votes on battles not involving the target shift Arena rankings, a manipulation of how pairwise votes are aggregated into a ranking.
Runs simulated users against conversational agents in a multi-agent evaluation framework, over synthetic policy-grounded scenarios generated from a policy graph.
Applies an agent-as-a-judge to check factual consistency of long-narrative summaries; the judge is the subject.

assignments.note: 2025-01 The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models
assignments.why: Compares PRM labelling methods, proposes consensus filtering and releases Qwen PRMs, and measures how Best-of-N evaluation hides PRMs drifting into outcome judges.

assignments.note: 2025-01 The alternative annotator test for LLM-as-a-judge
assignments.why: A statistical test for whether an LLM judge can replace human annotators, a meta-evaluation procedure for LLM judges.
Combines a human-preference reward model with verification agents (search for factuality, code checks for constraints) into one reward system.
A scientist model open-endedly generates new tasks against a novelty archive to probe a subject model's capabilities and failures, a generated test set.

assignments.note: 2025-02 Great models think alike and this undermines AI oversight
assignments.why: Introduces the CAPA similarity metric and measures that LLM judges favour similar models and that errors correlate as capability grows, an empirical judge-bias study.

assignments.note: 2025-02 If multi-agent debate is the answer what is the question
assignments.why: Systematic evaluation of multi-agent debate methods against chain-of-thought and self-consistency; debate is the paradigm under study.
A meta-evaluation benchmark of reward models and VLM judges on expert-annotated preference triplets.
Measures a contamination bias where LLM judges favour students trained on data from the same or related models.
Measures evaluator uncertainty across nine LLM judges and fine-tunes an uncertainty-aware judge (ConfiLM), with the judges' confidence as the main subject.

assignments.note: 2025-03 A benchmark for scalable oversight protocols
assignments.why: A benchmark and metric (agent score difference) for comparing oversight protocols such as debate and consultancy, i.e. meta-evaluation of non-single-judge paradigms.

assignments.note: 2025-03 Are Solved Issues in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly
assignments.why: Shows SWE-bench's verifier accepts wrong patches, using execution-based checks against full developer suites and generated differential tests (PatchDiff).
Measures backdoor vulnerability of evaluators by poisoning judge training data or weights, and tests model merging as a defence.
Uses Wald's SPRT and mSPRT to stop self-consistency sampling once one answer dominates, a sequential test applied to a consistency check.
Builds a hierarchical capability tree over benchmark instances to profile a model's weaknesses and guide targeted data collection, evaluating by weakness profile rather than one score.
Robustness meta-evaluation of LLM safety judges showing output-style changes shift false-negative rates by up to 0.24 though the content is the same.
Measures that LLM judges agree with experts mainly where they can answer themselves, and that expert references (reference-based judging) largely fix it.
Trains verbalized confidence with a strictly proper log-scoring-rule reward via PPO, a recipe for fine-tuning open 3B-9B LLMs into calibrated answerers.
Measures that apologetic-language artifacts skew 11 safety judges' preferences by up to 98% though the safety content is unchanged.
